# howler-audio-manager

> H5/Web audio management library built on howler.js: enum-driven preset sound effects, dual caching (effect cache + URL audio cache), singleton dynamic URL playback, overlap prevention, preload/preheat support, and a dual-layer event system that leaves no memory leaks.

This is a TypeScript library published as `@jswork/howler-audio-manager`. Business code supplies its own sound enum (generic `AudioManager<K>`); the library never hardcodes business keys or URLs. `howler` is a peer dependency; `react` (>=16.8) is an optional peer dependency used only by the React hooks exported from the main entry. Tests run with `bun test` (Howler is mocked, React hooks tested under happy-dom), and packages are built with tsup into ESM, CommonJS, and UMD formats.

## Source

- [Entry](src/index.ts): Public exports (AudioManager class, all types, and React hooks)
- [Core Implementation](src/manager.ts): AudioManager class — effects, URL audio, events, global controls, lifecycle
- [Type Definitions](src/types.ts): Play options, event payloads, subscriptions, and resource map contracts
- [React Hooks](src/react.tsx): AudioManagerProvider (Context) plus useAudio, useAudioEvent, useGlobalVolume, usePreload

## Tests

- [Test Suite](__tests__/index.spec.ts): Preset effects, dynamic URL audio, events, and lifecycle tests
- [React Hooks Tests](__tests__/react.spec.tsx): Provider, event subscription, volume sync, and preload state tests
- [Howler Mock](__tests__/mock-howler.ts): Deterministic Howl/Howler mock used by the test suite
- [Test Setup](__tests__/setup.ts): happy-dom global registration preloaded by bunfig.toml

## Configuration

- [Package Manifest](package.json): Dependencies (howler as peer dependency), scripts, and build entry points
- [Tsup Config](tsup.config.ts): Build pipeline producing ESM, CJS, and UMD bundles with type declarations
